title: XML: Support display string according to "encoding" attribute or the new "Default character encoding" preference
description:
# Summary

Support two enhancements:

1. Display character according to the "encoding" attribute of the XML declaration.

2. Add a new preference to set "Default character encoding" for some XML document without "encoding" attribute.

# Details
## Enhancement 1

This is a xml file with a "encoding" attribute of the XML declaration: [gb18030_with_encoding_attr.xml](/uploads/d7cb944404fa9df25e0864cf57939291/gb18030_with_encoding_attr.xml)

But XML dissector could not display the GB18030 character correctly:

![display_incorrectly_even_encoding_is_given](/uploads/1f962a354188ab4ed9c303837a77e0a5/display_incorrectly_even_encoding_is_given.png)

After adding enhancement 1 (the first enhancement), it displays correctly:

![display_correctly_according_to_encoding_attr](/uploads/27f4ee10c41ea7e7ca1fb9bd05881ca4/display_correctly_according_to_encoding_attr.png) 

## Enhancement 2

This is a xml file in GB18030 encoding, but without a "encoding" attribute in the XML declaration: [gb18030_without_encoding_attr.xml](/uploads/0c15bb71c3458b30f5725f51736bc085/gb18030_without_encoding_attr.xml)

XML dissector did not support setting default character encoding, so it was unable to display correctly:

![no_way_to_set_default_encoding](/uploads/96599fc68533f71506dfbcf950d642f0/no_way_to_set_default_encoding.png)

After adding enhancement 2 (the second enhancement), it displays correctly if the "Default character encoding" preference being set with "GB18030":

![display_correctly_with_default_encoding](/uploads/4309f2057971ab9ef8549f34ef51ebe4/display_correctly_with_default_encoding.png)

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 77027ccc - XML: Support display string according to "encoding" attribute or a preference
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10021/diffs?diff_id=625699096&start_sha=0a3d1266af9b8db7a3fa1323fe98afae60fcaf88)

Having this be a string preference instead of an enum preference is not ideal. The disadvantage of an enum preference is keeping it updated with what Wireshark supports, although perhaps it makes sense to have an `enum_val_t` for this purpose in `iana_charsets.h` or elsewhere.

(In the case of XML, we only need worry about IANA registered charsets and not the variety of other encodings that Wireshark supports, such as telephony encodings.)
That sounds like a really good idea. I will review the other MR when I get a chance.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10021/diffs?diff_id=636828787&start_sha=77027ccc0b7f0f9af1e3afbecba88c0c1f81c8fb#669b6534f8963572f5250bd89d5f04aebce6de31_1613_1614)

  • 77027ccc...1a290601 - 74 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • acb70562 - Support convert iana charset enum number of GB18030, GBK, GB2312
  • 19fedfff - iana_charsets: Define iana charsets enumeration and enum_val_t array
  • 96864feb - XML: Support display string according to "encoding" attribute or a preference
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10021/diffs?diff_id=636828787&start_sha=77027ccc0b7f0f9af1e3afbecba88c0c1f81c8fb)

I think this looks good. A couple thoughts come to mind, neither of which will block the MR from getting accepted, just about possible future improvements:

1. The encoding search only works for encodings that are ASCII compatible. We could use the first few bytes to guess that we have UTF-16 without BOM (00 3C 00 3F for UTF-16BE, for example), similar to how we test for a BOM. (Yes, it's supposed to have a BOM when using UTF-16, but it might not.)
2. Weird things happen if the document has a UTF-8 compatible initial header and encoding tag and then claims to be UTF-16. Maybe eventually we should warn about that with an expert info.
3. The xml dissector is added to the media type dissector. The media type can also have a `charset` parameter. Maybe we should check for that too (this also applies to other media type dissectors too.)

Finally, we might want to detect UTF-8 or GB18030 XML documents that have been converted from UTF-16 and thus contain a translated U+FEFF BYTE ORDER MARK at the beginning. As files, those aren't recognized as XML files because the heuristic dissector doesn't check for those kinds of BOMs, even though the XML spec does specifically allow UTF-8 entities to have BOMs at the start.

commits_data.title: XML: Support display string according to "encoding" attribute or a preference
commits_data.message:
XML: Support display string according to "encoding" attribute or a preference

Display character according to the "encoding" attribute of the XML
declaration. Add a new preference to set default character encoding
for some XML document without "encoding" attribute.
